Surah al-An'am (The Cattle) [Meccan, except verses 20, 23, 91, 93, 114, 141, 151, 152 and 153, which are Medinan; its number of verses is 165]

﴿Praise be to Allah﴾: al-hamd (praise) is the attribution of beauty, and it is established ﴿for Allah﴾. Is the purpose of this [statement] to inform [people] of it so that they believe in it, or to glorify Him by it, or both? There are possibilities; the most beneficial of them is the third, as stated by al-Shaykh (al-Mahalli) in Surat al-Kahf. ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth﴾: He specified these two for mention because they are the greatest of the creations for those who look. ﴿And made﴾ (created) ﴿the darknesses and the light﴾: that is, every darkness and every light; He gathered them in the plural without [mentioning] the others because of the multiplicity of their causes. This is among the proofs of His oneness. ﴿Yet those who disbelieve﴾, despite the presence of this proof, ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾: they make others equal to Him in worship.

He it is Who created you from clay, by creating your father Adam from it. Then He decreed a term, a term for you [at the end of which] you will die. And there is a specified term with Him, [a term] fixed for your resurrection. Then you, O disbelievers, are in doubt, [you] are uncertain about the resurrection, despite your knowledge that He originated your creation, and that whoever is able to originate is even more able to restore.

﴿And He is Allah﴾ deserving of worship ﴿in the heavens and the earth. He knows your secret and your open⁠ [speech]﴾ what you conceal and what you disclose among yourselves ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾ what you do of good and evil.

Translation:

﴿And no sign comes to them﴾ — i.e., the people of Makkah — ﴿from﴾ (the "min" is extra/emphatic) ﴿the signs of their Lord﴾ — from the Qur'an.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah al-An'am, verse 5:

﴿Indeed they have denied the truth﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿when it came to them. So there will come to them the news﴾ — the consequences (ʿawāqib).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 6:

﴿Have they not seen﴾ in their journeys to al-Sham (Syria) and elsewhere ﴿how many﴾ (kam khabariyyah, meaning "many") ﴿generations We destroyed before them﴾, a community from the past nations, ﴿whom We had established﴾ We gave them a place ﴿on the earth, [with a power and an extent] that We have not established﴾ We have not given ﴿for you﴾ here there is a shift (iltifat) from the third person (ghaybah) ﴿and We sent the sky﴾ the rain ﴿upon them in abundance﴾ continuously ﴿and made the rivers flow beneath them﴾ beneath their dwellings ﴿then We destroyed them for their sins﴾ by their denial of the prophets.

﴿And if We had sent down to you a book﴾ written ﴿on paper﴾, a parchment (*raqq*), as they had proposed, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, which is more conclusive than those who witnessed it seeing it, because that removes doubt more effectively, ﴿the disbelievers would have said, "This is nothing but clear magic"﴾. The word *in* (إنْ) here means *ma* (ما), i.e., "this is not", and the disbelievers' words are said out of obstinacy and stubborn defiance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 8:

﴿And they say: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?"﴾ That is, "Why not (هَلّا, hallā)" — sent down to him, to Muhammad (ﷺ), an angel ﴿who would confirm him﴾.

﴿But if We had sent down an angel﴾, as they proposed, and they did not believe, ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ by their destruction, ﴿and then they would not be reprieved﴾, meaning they would not be given respite for repentance or an excuse. This is in accordance with God's custom regarding those before them: when the thing they demanded occurs and they do not believe, He destroys them.

﴿And if We had made him﴾, i.e., the one sent down to them, ﴿an angel, We would have made him﴾, i.e., the angel, ﴿a man﴾, i.e., in his form, so that they could be able to see him, since humans have no strength to see an angel. ﴿And﴾ if We had sent him down and made him a man, ﴿We would have confused for them﴾, i.e., We would have made confusing to them, ﴿what they confuse﴾ over themselves, by saying: ﴿This is none other than a human being like yourselves﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 10:

﴿And indeed, messengers before you were ridiculed.﴾ In this there is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿Then there descended﴾ (fa-ḥāqa): it came down upon ﴿those who mocked them, that which they used to ridicule.﴾ That is the punishment. Thus it likewise befalls those who ridicule you.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 11:

﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿Travel through the earth and then observe how was the end of those who denied﴾ the messengers, [namely] their destruction through punishment, ﴿so that they may take heed﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 12:

﴿Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?" Say, "To Allah."﴾ If they do not say it, there is no other answer. ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy.﴾ He decreed for Himself (qaḍā ʿalā nafsihi), as a bounty from Him, and in it is gentleness in calling them to faith. ﴿He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection,﴾ to recompense you for your deeds. ﴿About which there is no doubt (rayb),﴾ i.e., no uncertainty (shakk). ﴿Those who have lost their souls,﴾ by exposing them to punishment, are the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿so they do not believe.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 13:

﴿And to Him belongs﴾ — He, the Exalted — ﴿whatever dwells﴾ — rests, settles — ﴿in the night and the day﴾. That is, everything; so He is its Lord, its Creator, and its Owner. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what is said, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what is done.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 14:

﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿Shall I take as a protector other than Allah﴾ whom I worship, ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, its Creator and Innovator, ﴿while He feeds﴾ provides sustenance, ﴿and is not fed﴾ is not provided for. ﴿Say﴾ "Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾ to Allah from this nation, ﴿and﴾ it was said to me, ﴿Do not be among the polytheists﴾ associating others with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 15:

﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord,﴾ by worshipping other than Him, ﴿the punishment of a tremendous Day."﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Whoever is spared it (al-ʿadhab, the punishment) on that Day, Allah has surely shown him mercy﴾ — the verb ﴿yuṣraf﴾ is read in the passive (with al-ʿadhāb as its implied subject), and in the active (with Allah as subject), and the returning pronoun (al-ʾāʾid) is omitted: the full sense is ﴿yuṣraf ʿanhu﴾. ﴿ʿAnhu yawmaʾidhin faqad raḥimahu﴾ — that is, He willed good for him, ﴿and that is the manifest triumph﴾, the clear deliverance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 17:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾, such as affliction, illness or poverty, ﴿there is none to remove it except Him﴾, none to lift it; ﴿and if He touches you with good﴾, such as health and wealth, ﴿then He is over all things Powerful﴾. And from this is His touching you with good, and no one other than Him can turn it away from you.

﴿And He is the Subjugator﴾ , the Able, whom nothing can render incapable, exalted ﴿above His servants﴾. ﴿And He is the All-Wise﴾ in His creation, ﴿the All-Aware﴾ of their inward states as of their outward ones.

It was revealed when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Bring us someone who will testify for you to prophethood, for the People of the Book have denied you." ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"What thing is greatest as testimony?"﴾ (tamyīz, a specifier transferred from the subject) ﴿Say: "God"﴾, if they do not say it, there is no other answer. ﴿He is a witness between me and you﴾ to my truthfulness. ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you﴾, I frighten you, O people of Makkah, ﴿by it, and whomever it reaches﴾ (conjoined to the pronoun in "that I may warn you"), i.e., by the message of the Qur'an, from among mankind and the jinn. ﴿Do you really testify that there are other gods with God?﴾ (an interrogative of denial). ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"I do not testify"﴾ to that. ﴿Say: "He is only one God, and I am innocent of what you associate"﴾ with Him of idols.

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognise him﴾, i.e., Muhammad (ﷺ), by his description in their scripture, ﴿as they recognise their own sons. Those who have lost their souls﴾ from among them, ﴿they do not believe﴾ in him.

﴿وَمَن﴾ i.e., no one ﴿is more unjust than he who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by attributing a partner to Him, ﴿or denies His signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, it is so that the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ in that.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 22:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who ascribed partners [to God]﴾ as a rebuke, ﴿"Where are your partners whom you used to claim﴾ [were partners of God]?"﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 23:

﴿Then their trial (fitnatahum)﴾ — read with ta' and ya' (tukun and yakun) — ﴿would not be﴾ — with the accusative and nominative readings for "fitnatahum" — meaning their excuse (ma'dhiratahum), ﴿except that they said﴾ — i.e., their saying — ﴿"By Allah, our Lord"﴾ — with the genitive reading, as an adjective (na't), and the accusative reading as a vocative (nida').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 24:

﴿Look﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿how they lied against themselves﴾ by denying their polytheism, ﴿and what they used to invent﴾, that which they used to fabricate against Allah concerning partners, ﴿has deserted them﴾, i.e., has disappeared from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 25:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ when you recite; ﴿and We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ (aghtiya, veils) ﴿lest they understand it﴾ i.e., lest they comprehend the Qur'an; ﴿and in their ears is deafness﴾ (samamun, deafness), so they do not hear it with the hearing of acceptance. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; until, when they come to you, they dispute with you, those who disbelieve say: "This is not﴾ (ma, not) ﴿anything but the fables of the ancients﴾ (akadhib, lies, like the amusing tales and marvels); ʾasatir is the plural of ʾusturah, with a dammah on the alif.

Translation of the passage:

It is said: it was revealed concerning Abu Talib, who used to forbid people from harming him (ﷺ) while not believing in him. ﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾, because its harm falls upon them, ﴿yet they perceive it not﴾ in that regard.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 27:

﴿And if you could see﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿when they are made to stand﴾ before ﴿the Fire, and they will say: "Oh, would that we could be returned"﴾ to the world ﴿and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ The verbs are read with raised endings as a resumed statement (isti'naf), and with subjunctive endings as an answer to the wish (tamanni); the first is raised and the second is in the subjunctive. Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 36:

﴿Only those who hear⦆ ... 

Translation:

"Only those who listen" (the Qur'anic words "Only those who hear will respond") — the response here means responding to your call (du'a'aka) to faith, ﴿those who hear﴾ with the hearing of understanding and reflection, ﴿and the dead﴾ — i.e., the disbelievers, whom He likened to the dead in their failure to hear — ﴿God will raise them﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿then to Him they will be returned﴾, they will be sent back, and He will recompense them for their deeds.

And they say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" (i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah; "why not" means "would that," such as the she-camel, the staff, and the table). Say, "Indeed Allah is able to send down a sign," (the verb nazzala may be read with the doubled or single letter), of what they have proposed, "but most of them do not know" that sending it down would be a trial for them, since their destruction would become obligatory if they denied it.

"And there is no creature moving on the earth, nor a bird flying with its two wings, but they are communities like you"—[the word] "min" [here] is extra (za'ida)—"in their arrangement, their provision and their conditions. We have not neglected"—we have not left out—"in the Book," the Preserved Tablet, "anything," so We have not failed to record it. "Then to their Lord they will be gathered," whereupon He will judge between them and exact retribution for the hornless [sheep] from the horned, then He will say to them, "Be dust!"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 39:

﴿Those who denied Our signs﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿are deaf﴾ to hearing them with acceptance, ﴿and dumb﴾ from speaking the truth, ﴿in darknesses﴾, i.e., disbelief. ﴿Whomever Allah wills﴾, i.e., to send astray, ﴿He sends astray; and whomever He wills﴾, i.e., to guide, ﴿He places him upon a path﴾, i.e., a way, ﴿straight﴾, i.e., the religion of Islam.

Say (O Muhammad, to the people of Makkah): "Tell me, [if] the punishment of Allah comes upon you in this world, or the Hour comes upon you suddenly, the Hour that includes it, would you call upon other than Allah? [Answer:] No, [you would not]. [Say:] If you are truthful in your claim that the idols benefit you, then call upon them."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 41:

﴿Rather, it is Him﴾ not other than Him ﴿you call upon﴾ in times of adversity, ﴿and He removes that for which you call upon Him﴾ that He remove it from you, the harm and the like, ﴿if He wills﴾ to remove it, ﴿and you forget﴾ you leave aside ﴿what you associate﴾ with Him of idols, so you do not call upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 42:

﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you,﴾ [the word] "min" (from) is extra (zā'ida) ﴿before you,﴾ messengers, and they denied them, ﴿so We seized them with adversity﴾ severity of poverty ﴿and hardship﴾ sickness, ﴿that perhaps they might humble themselves﴾ abase themselves, ﴿and so believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 47:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Tell me, if God's punishment comes upon you suddenly or openly﴾ by night or by day, ﴿will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people﴾ the disbelievers. That is, none will be destroyed except them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 48:

﴿And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good news﴾ to those who believe in Paradise, ﴿and warners﴾ to those who disbelieve, with the Fire. ﴿So whoever believes﴾ in them ﴿and reforms﴾ his deed, ﴿there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿And those who denied Our signs, the punishment will touch them for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾ They go out of obedience.

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah"﴾, from which He gives provision, ﴿"nor"﴾ that I ﴿know the unseen"﴾, meaning what is hidden from me and has not been revealed to me. ﴿"Nor do I tell you that I am an angel"﴾ from among the angels, ﴿"I follow only what is revealed to me."﴾ ﴿Say: "Are the blind"﴾, meaning the disbeliever, ﴿"and the seeing"﴾, meaning the believer, ﴿"equal? Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 51:

﴿And warn﴾ frighten ﴿with it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿no protector﴾ who will help them ﴿nor intercessor﴾ who will intercede for them.
