Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 52:

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Face﴾ by their worship, ﴿His Face﴾ (Exalted is He), not anything of the goods of this world. They are the poor. The polytheists had reviled them and demanded that he drive them away so that they might sit with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wished this, out of eagerness for their Islam. ﴿You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way﴾, the word "min" here being extra (ziyadah), ﴿in any way﴾, if their inner state is not pleasing. ﴿Nor are they accountable for your reckoning in any way, so that you would drive them away﴾, this being the answer to the negation, ﴿and thereby you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ if you did that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 53:

﴿And thus did We test﴾ [We tried] ﴿some of them by means of others﴾, i.e., the noble by the lowly and the rich by the poor, by placing the former before the latter in the race to faith ﴿so that they say﴾, i.e., the nobles and the rich, in denial, ﴿"Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾ — the poor — ﴿[He has guided them, i.e., if what they are upon were guidance, they would not have preceded us to it]. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ to Him, so that He guides them?" [Yes, He is.]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 54:

﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say﴾ to them, ﴿"Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy, that﴾ i.e., indeed, the matter is that ﴿whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾ on his part, in that he commits it, ﴿then repents﴾ returns (to Allah) ﴿after it﴾ after his deed, ﴿and makes amends﴾ his deed, ﴿then indeed He﴾ i.e., Allah ﴿is Forgiving﴾ to him ﴿and Merciful﴾ to him. And in another reading with a fatḥah (on the initial letter of ﴿أنَّهُ﴾, i.e., ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾), it is a substitute for ﴿الرَّحْمَة﴾ (mercy), i.e., the forgiveness is for him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 55:

﴿And thus﴾ as We have explained what has been mentioned, ﴿We detail﴾ We make clear ﴿the verses﴾ of the Qur'an, so that the truth may become manifest and be acted upon, ﴿and that the way﴾ the path ﴿of the criminals﴾ may become evident, so that it is avoided. In one reading it is read with the yaʾ (third person masculine), and in another with the tāʾ (second person feminine), and the accusative of ﴿way﴾ is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 56:

﴿Say: "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon"﴾ [you worship] ﴿besides Allah.﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in their worship ﴿for then I would have gone astray﴾ if I followed them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 57:

﴿Say: "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence (bayyina) from my Lord, and you have denied it."﴾ Bayyina here means a clear proof. ﴿And you have denied it﴾ — and indeed you have denied your Lord by associating partners with Him. ﴿What you are hastening for is not with me.﴾ That is, the punishment. ﴿The judgment is not but for Allah﴾ — regarding that and other matters; ﴿He relates the truth (yaqussu al-haqq)﴾ — that is, He narrates the decision (al-qada') with truth; ﴿and He is the best of those who decide (al-fasilin)﴾ — the best of those who judge (al-hakimin). And in another reading, yaqussu means yaqulu, i.e., "He says."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 58:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿If I had that for which you are impatient [i.e., the punishment] within my power, the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾ by my hastening it for you, so that I might find rest. But it is with God, ﴿and God knows best the wrongdoers﴾, as to when He will punish them.

And with Him (Exalted is He) are **the keys of the unseen** (*mafatih al-ghayb*), meaning His treasuries, or the means that lead to His knowledge. **None knows them but He.** They are the five [matters] mentioned in His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah has with Him the knowledge of the Hour﴾ (Luqman 31:34), and the verse [continues], as al-Bukhari narrated. **And He knows what is** in **the land** (*al-barr*, the deserts) **and the sea** (*al-bahr*, the towns that lie along the rivers). **And not a leaf falls** but that He knows it, **nor a grain** [falls] **in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry** (*ruṭb wa-la yābis*), [the latter] conjoined to *waraqa* (leaf), **but it is in a Clear Record**, which is the **Preserved Tablet** (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*). The exception here is a substitution of inclusion (*badal ishtimal*, a substitute that includes what it replaces) from the exception preceding it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 60:

﴿It is He who takes you back [in death] at night⁠﴾ — He seizes your souls during sleep. ﴿And He knows what you have earned⁠﴾ — what you have committed ﴿by day. Then He revives you therein⁠﴾ — i.e., during the day, by returning your souls. ﴿That a specified term may be fulfilled⁠﴾ — which is the term of life. ﴿Then to Him is your return⁠﴾ — by resurrection. ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do⁠﴾ — and then He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 61:

﴿And He is the Subduer﴾ (al-Qahir), exalted ﴿over His servants. And He sends over you guardians﴾ (hafazah), angels who record your deeds, ﴿until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him up﴾ (tawaffathu), and in another reading tawaffahu, ﴿Our messengers﴾, the angels entrusted with seizing souls, ﴿and they do not fail﴾ (la yufarrituna), meaning they do not fall short in what they are commanded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 62:

﴿Then they are returned﴾ i.e., the creation, ﴿to God, their Master (mawla)﴾ their Owner, ﴿the Truth﴾ the Established, the Just, so that He may recompense them. ﴿Verily, His is the judgment﴾ the binding decree concerning them, ﴿and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾ He will reckon with all of creation in the span of about half a day of the days of this world, according to a hadith to that effect.

Say (O Muhammad, to the people of Makkah): "Who delivers you from the darknesses of the land and the sea," i.e., their terrors, during your journeys, when ﴿you call upon Him humbly﴾ openly ﴿and secretly﴾ privately, saying: ﴿"If He delivers us from this,"﴾ the lam here is a lam of oath, ﴿"we will surely be among the thankful,"﴾ the believers. In another reading, it is "anjānā" (He delivered us), i.e., Allah, ﴿from this﴾ darkness and hardship.

Say, [O Muhammad, to them]: "Allah delivers you from it [the distress at sea] and from every affliction [other than it, i.e., any grief]," yet then you associate others with Him.

[Note on the reading: "yunajjikum" is read with both the light (takhfif) and the heavy (tashdid) forms of the letter jim.]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 65:

﴿Say: He is the One able to send upon you punishment from above you﴾ from the sky, like stones and the Shout (al-sayha), ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ like the earthquake (al-khasf), ﴿or to confuse you﴾ mix you, ﴿in sects﴾ groups of differing inclinations, ﴿and make you taste the violence of one another﴾ through fighting. He (ﷺ) said, when this was revealed: "This is easier and lighter," and when what preceded it was revealed he said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." Narrated by al-Bukhari. Muslim related the hadith: "I asked my Lord that He not make the violence of my community fall upon one another, and He denied me this." And in another hadith: "When it was revealed he said: Indeed it will occur, but its interpretation has not yet come." ﴿Behold how We vary the signs﴾ We make clear to them ﴿the signs﴾ the proofs of Our power, ﴿that they may understand﴾ know that what they are upon is false.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 66:

﴿And your people denied it﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿though it is the truth﴾, meaning the true thing. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿I am not a guardian over you﴾, so that I would requite you. Rather, I am only a warner, and your affair is up to Allah. This was before the command to fight.

For every news there is a time when it will be settled (Tafsir al-Jalalayn). Qur'anic quotation: ﴿For every news there is a time of settlement﴾.

Here is the translation of the passage:

﴿For every news﴾: a report; ﴿a time of settlement﴾: a time at which it occurs and becomes fixed, and among it is your punishment. ﴿And you will soon know﴾: a threat to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 68:

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses﴾, [i.e., the Qur'an] with mockery, ﴿then turn away from them﴾ and do not sit with them, ﴿until they engage in talk about something else. And if﴾ there is an assimilation here, of the nūn of the conditional particle in (in) into the added mā (in ma), ﴿Satan causes you to forget﴾ (with the nūn sukūn and lightened, and with its fatḥah and emphasized), ﴿then do not sit, after the remembrance﴾, i.e., the reminder, ﴿with the wrongdoing people﴾. Here the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun. And the Muslims said: If we stand up whenever they engage in vain talk, we will not be able to sit in the mosque and circumambulate [the Ka'bah]. So it was revealed:

Note: the Arabic words being discussed (يُنْسِيَنك, فِيهِ إدْغام, وإمّا) are transliterated here as yunsiyannaka (with the nūn sukūn and lightened, and with its fatḥah and emphasized), and in ma (the nūn of in assimilated into the added mā), as they appear in the commentary.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 69:

﴿And upon those who fear (Allah) there is nothing of their reckoning﴾ (Allah) ﴿i.e., of those who engage in vain discourse﴾, ﴿min﴾ is extra (ziyada) ﴿anything﴾ if they sit with them; ﴿but﴾ upon them (is) ﴿a reminder﴾, an admonition and a warning for them ﴿so that they may fear﴾ the vain discourse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 70:

﴿And leave﴾ (utruk) ﴿those who have taken their religion﴾ which they were charged with ﴿as amusement and diversion﴾ by their mockery of it, ﴿and whom the worldly life has deceived﴾, so do not confront them. This was before the command to fight.

﴿And remind﴾ (ʿiz, admonish) ﴿by it﴾, by the Qur'an, ﴿the people﴾, ﴿lest a soul be given over to destruction﴾ (tusbala nafs, delivered up to ruin) ﴿for what it has earned﴾ (ʿamilat, done). ﴿It will have no protector﴾ (waliyy, helper) ﴿besides Allah, nor any intercessor﴾ who would prevent punishment from it. ﴿And if it offers every ransom﴾ (taʿdil kulla ʿadl, tafdi kulla fidaʾ), ﴿it will not be accepted from it.﴾ ﴿Those are the ones delivered up to destruction for what they earned. For them is a drink of boiling water﴾ (ma' bāligh nihāyat al-ḥarāra, water that has reached the utmost of heat) ﴿and a painful punishment﴾ (muʾlim, painful) ﴿for what they used to deny﴾, meaning for their disbelief.

Say: "Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have led astray in the earth, bewildered, having companions who call him to guidance, saying: 'Come to us'?" Say: "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (true) guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."

Commentary:

Say (Allah's command to the Prophet ﷺ): "Shall we worship, besides Allah, that which neither benefits us by our worshipping it nor harms us by our abandoning it" — and that is the idols — "and be turned back on our heels" — that is, return as polytheists — "after Allah has guided us" — to Islam — "like one whom the devils have led astray" — made him lose his way — "in the earth, bewildered," — perplexed, not knowing where to go; this is a state (ḥāl) relating to the pronoun in "lahu" (his) — "having companions" — a group of fellow travellers — "who call him to guidance" — that is, they want to guide him to the path, saying to him: "Come to us," so he does not answer them and perishes. The interrogative is for denunciation, and the clause of the simile is a state (ḥāl) relating to the pronoun in "nuradd" (we are turned back).

"Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah" — which is Islam — "is the (true) guidance," and whatever is other than it is misguidance. "And we have been commanded to submit" — that is, that we should submit.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 72:

﴿And﴾ i.e., [we were commanded] that ﴿establish the prayer and fear Him﴾ (exalted is He), ﴿and it is He to whom you will be gathered﴾, i.e., you will be brought together on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning.

And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth, i.e., justly (muhiqqan). [And mention] the Day He says to a thing, "Be," and it is. That is the Day of Resurrection; He says to the creation, "Rise," and they rise. His word is the truth (al-haqq), the true statement that will certainly come to pass. His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown (al-sur), the Horn; the second blast, from Israfil. No dominion will belong to anyone else on that Day. "To whom belongs the dominion today?" "To Allah," [the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed], meaning what is hidden and what is observed. And He is the All-Wise in His creation, the All-Aware of the inner reality of things as of their outward appearance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 74:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. He is his epithet (laqab); his name was Tarikh. ﴿Do you take idols as gods?﴾ that you worship them. It is an interrogative of reproach. ﴿Indeed I see you and your people﴾ in taking them ﴿in clear error﴾ away from the truth, ﴿evident﴾, clear.

﴿And thus﴾ as We showed [the reality of] his father's and his people's misguidance, ﴿We showed Abraham the dominion [malakut]﴾ meaning the kingdom ﴿of the heavens and the earth﴾, so that he might reason by it to Our oneness, ﴿and that he might be among the certain﴾ in it. The sentence beginning "and thus" and what follows it is an i'tiraD (a parenthetical insertion, an interjected clause), and it is conjoined (ʿuṭifa) to "he said" (qāla).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 76:

﴿When night covered him﴾ grew dark over him, ﴿the night, he saw a star﴾ it is said it was Venus, ﴿and said﴾ to his people, who were astrologers, ﴿"This is my lord"﴾ according to your claim, ﴿then when it set﴾ disappeared, ﴿he said, "I do not love those that set"﴾ that I should take them as lords, because the Lord may not be subject to change and movement, since these are the attributes of created things. ﴿So it did not benefit them that.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 77:

﴿So when he saw the moon rising﴾, shining forth, ﴿he said﴾ to them: ﴿"This is my lord." But when it set, he said: "Unless my lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who are astray."﴾ That is, "Unless my lord keeps me firm upon guidance." ﴿"I will surely be among the people who are astray"﴾ was an allusion to his people, that they were in error; but that did not benefit them.

When he saw the sun rising brightly, he said: "This is my Lord; this is greater." [He said this] to remind them of his story (dhakarahu li-tadhkirihi khabarahu). ﴿This is my Lord; this is greater.﴾ [Greater] than the star and the moon. ﴿Then when it set﴾ and his argument prevailed over them, and they did not return, ﴿he said: "O my people, I am free from what you associate [with Allah]"﴾ of idols and bodies that are originated (al-ajram al-muhdatha), which are in need of an originator (muhdith). So they said to him: "What do you worship?"

He said, ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face﴾, meaning I directed my worship ﴿to Him who originated﴾, that is, created, ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, namely Allah, ﴿as a ḥanīf﴾ (inclining away from falsehood toward the true religion), ﴿inclined toward the upright religion﴾. ﴿And I am not of those who associate [others with Him]﴾, meaning with Him.

﴿And his people argued with him.﴾ They disputed with him about his religion and threatened him with the idols, that they would afflict him with harm if he abandoned them.

﴿He said: "Do you argue with me..."﴾ The word أتُحاجُّونَنِي is read with the nun doubled (تشديد النون) and also with the nun reduced (تخفيفها) by deleting one of the two nuns. According to the grammarians, the deleted nun is نون الرفع (nun al-rafʿ, the nun of the verb's grammatical ending), and according to the reciters it is نون الوقاية (nun al-wiqayah, the protective nun). The meaning is: أتُجادِلُونَنِي, "Do you dispute with me..."

﴿concerning God﴾, that is, concerning His oneness, ﴿when He has guided me﴾ to it, ﴿and I do not fear what you associate﴾, and I do not fear what you associate with Him of idols, that they might afflict me with harm, because they have no power over anything, ﴿except that my Lord wills something﴾ of the disliked matter that might afflict me, and so it happens. ﴿My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾, that is, His knowledge encompasses all things. ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ of this, so that you would believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 81:

﴿How should I fear what you associate﴾ with Allah, when it neither harms nor benefits, ﴿while you do not fear﴾ from Allah ﴿that you have associated with Allah﴾ in worship ﴿that for which He has not sent down﴾ by worshipping it ﴿any authority upon you﴾, meaning proof and evidence, ﴿and He is the Able over everything﴾. ﴿So which of the two groups is more deserving of security﴾, we or you ﴿if you know﴾ who is more deserving of it? That is, it is we, so follow us.

﴿Those who believe and do not mix﴾ (yalbisū) their belief ﴿with wrongdoing﴾ — i.e., with shirk (association of partners with God), as it was explained in the hadith in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) — ﴿those will have security﴾ from punishment.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 83:

﴿That﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿Our argument﴾ is a substitute (badal) for it, namely the argument which Ibrahim (Abraham) used to prove the Oneness of God from the setting of the star and what follows it. The predicate (khabar) is ﴿We gave it to Ibrahim﴾, meaning: We guided him to it as an argument ﴿against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will﴾, with the iḍāfa (genitive construction) and the tanwīn (nunation) readings, in knowledge and wisdom. ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise﴾ in His creation, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of His creatures.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 84:

﴿And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob﴾, his son, ﴿each of them We guided, and Noah We guided before, and of his offspring﴾, i.e., Noah's offspring, ﴿David and Solomon﴾, his son, ﴿and Job and Joseph﴾, son of Jacob, ﴿and Moses and Aaron. And thus﴾, as We recompensed them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 85:

﴿And Zakariyya (Zechariah) and Yahya (John)﴾ his son, ﴿and Isa (Jesus)﴾ son of Maryam (Mary). This indicates that the dhurriyyah (offspring, descendants) includes the children of a daughter. ﴿And Ilyas (Elias)﴾ son of the brother of Harun (Aaron), the brother of Musa (Moses). ﴿Each one﴾ of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 86:

﴿And Isma'il﴾, the son of Ibrahim, ﴿and al-Yasa'﴾ — the lam is extra (zā'idah) — ﴿and Yunus and Lut﴾, the son of Haran, the brother of Ibrahim, ﴿and each﴾ of them ﴿We preferred over the worlds﴾ by prophethood.

(Verse 87:) ﴿And from among their fathers, their descendants and their brothers⦆ — it is conjoined to "each" (kullan) or to "Noah," and "from among" (min) is partitive, because some of them had no offspring, and some of them had an unbelieving son among their descendants. ﴿And We chose them⦆ — We selected them.
﴿That﴾ the religion to which they were guided ﴿is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated [others with Him]﴾ hypothetically.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 89:

﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book﴾, meaning the books (al-kutub), ﴿and the judgment﴾, meaning the wisdom (al-hikmah), ﴿and prophethood. So if these [people of Makkah] disbelieve in them﴾, i.e., in these three, ﴿then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them﴾, i.e., We have appointed for them a people, namely the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 90:

﴿Those are the ones whom God guided﴾, that is, they are the ones ﴿God guided﴾. ﴿So follow their guidance﴾, meaning their way, which consists of monotheism (tawhid) and patience. ﴿Follow﴾, with the silent ha (ha' al-sakt, the pronoun-ending ha that is pronounced when the word is paused on or joined to what follows) in ﴿iqtadihi﴾ kept both in pause and in connection. In one reading, it is dropped when connected. ﴿Say﴾ to the people of Makkah: ﴿I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾, that is, for the Qur'an, ﴿a reward﴾ that you would give me. ﴿It is not but a reminder﴾, that is, the Qur'an is nothing but an admonition, ﴿to the worlds﴾, meaning mankind and the jinn.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 91:

﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾ i.e., the Jews did not magnify Him with His true magnificence, or did not know Him with His true knowing, ﴿when they said﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ, and they had disputed with him about the Qur'an, ﴿"God did not send down anything upon a human being."﴾ Say ﴿"Who sent down the Book which Moses brought, a light and guidance for mankind, which you make into scrolls"﴾ (reading yaj'alunahu with ya' and ta' in the three places) ﴿"scrolls"﴾ i.e., you write it on separate sheets ﴿"which you display"﴾ i.e., what you like to show of them, ﴿"and conceal much"﴾ of what is in them, such as the description of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿"And you were taught"﴾ O Jews, through the Qur'an, ﴿"what neither you nor your fathers knew"﴾ of the Torah, by clarifying what was confused for you and about which you differed. ﴿Say: "God."﴾ He sent it down, if they do not say so, there is no other answer. ﴿Then leave them in their idle talk﴾, their falsehood.

This is the Qur'an, a Book We have sent down, blessed, confirming what came before it [of the Books], **[and]** that you may warn (the reading is with both ta' and ya', and it is conjoined to the meaning of what precedes it, i.e., We sent it down for blessing and confirmation, and that you may warn by it) the Mother of Cities (i.e., the people of Makkah) and those around it (i.e., all other people). Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are watchful over their prayers, fearing its punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 93:

﴿And who⁠ ﴾ i.e., no one ﴿does greater wrong than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by claiming prophethood when he has not been appointed a prophet, ﴿or says, "It has been revealed to me," when nothing has been revealed to him﴾. It was revealed concerning Musaylima. ﴿Or one who says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed"﴾. They are the mockers, who said, "If we wished, we would say the like of this." ﴿If only you could see﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾ mentioned here ﴿are in the agonies﴾ i.e., the pangs ﴿of death, and the angels are stretching out their hands﴾ toward them, with blows and torment, saying to them in reproach, ﴿"Release your souls! Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾ i.e., disgrace ﴿for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth﴾ by claiming prophethood and revelation falsely, ﴿and you used to disdain His signs﴾ i.e., you used to be arrogant about believing in them. The answer to "if only you could see" is: a dreadful matter.

[And] it will be said to them when they are resurrected: "Indeed you have come to Us alone (furada), individually, separated from family, wealth and children, ﴿just as We created you the first time﴾, i.e., barefoot, naked and uncircumcised (ghurlan). ﴿And you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾, i.e., what We gave you of wealth, ﴿behind your backs﴾, in the world, not by your choice." ﴿And﴾ it will be said to them as a rebuke: ﴿"We do not see with you your intercessors"﴾, the idols, ﴿"whom you claimed to be among you"﴾, i.e., in deserving your worship, ﴿"as partners"﴾ to God. ﴿"Surely your bonds have been severed among you"﴾, i.e., your union has been scattered; and in another reading with the accusative, as an adverbial of time (zarf), meaning "your union has been severed between you." ﴿"And there has gone astray"﴾, i.e., there has vanished ﴿"from you what you used to claim"﴾ in the world regarding their intercession.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 95:

﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter﴾ [i.e., the one who cleaves] ﴿of the grain﴾ [seed] ﴿and the date-stone﴾ [i.e., cleaving them] ﴿to bring forth vegetation﴾ [i.e., cleaving the grain to bring forth plants] and [cleaving] the date-stone [to bring forth the palm tree]. ﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾ [like the human being and the bird from the sperm-drop and the egg]. ﴿And brings the dead out of the living﴾ [the sperm-drop and the egg]. ﴿That is Allah﴾ [the one who splits and brings forth]. ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ [How are you turned away] from faith [when the proof is established?]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 96:

﴿Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ﴾ (the Cleaver of the daybreak), a verbal noun meaning the dawn, i.e., the One who splits the column of the morning, which is the first thing that appears of the light of day out of the darkness of night. ﴿And He made the night a stillness﴾ in which creatures rest from fatigue. ﴿And the sun and the moon﴾ in the accusative, as a conjunction with the place (maḥall) of "the night." ﴿A reckoning﴾, a calculation of the times; or the preposition (bāʾ) is omitted, and it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from an implied subject, i.e., they run with a reckoning, as in the verse of al-Raḥmān: ﴿The sun and the moon [run] by a reckoning﴾ [[﴿ٱلشَّمۡسُ وٱلۡقَمَرُ بِحُسۡبانࣲ (٥)﴾]]. ﴿That﴾ mentioned [is] ﴿the decree of the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Knowing﴾ of His creation.

He it is who made the stars for you, that you might be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea, [i.e., during journeys]. We have indeed detailed the signs [i.e., the proofs] of Our power for a people who know [i.e., who reflect].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 98:

﴿And it is He who produced you﴾ created you ﴿from one soul﴾ which is Adam ﴿and [for you is] a place of residence﴾ for some of you in the womb ﴿and a place of storage﴾ for some of you in the loins (ṣulb). And in another reading, with a fatḥah on the qāf, meaning a place of settling (makān qarār) for you. ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾ what is said to them.

And He it is who sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth with it (﴿فَأَخْرَجْنا﴾). Here there is an *iltifat* (shift from the third person, *al-ghayba*, to the first person). **(*iltifat*: a shift in grammatical person within a single discourse.)** ﴿With it﴾, meaning with the water, ﴿the vegetation of every thing﴾ that grows. ﴿Then We bring forth from it﴾, that is, from the vegetation, ﴿something green﴾, in the sense of *akhdar* (green). ﴿From it We bring forth﴾, from the green, ﴿grain layered upon grain﴾, where some of it rests upon other parts, like the ears of wheat and the like. ﴿And from the palm﴾ is a *khabar* (predicate), and it may be substituted by *badal* (apposition) for the preceding phrase, ﴿from its spathe﴾, that is, what first emerges from it, and the subject (*mubtada'*) is ﴿clusters﴾, meaning strings of dates, ﴿hanging low﴾, meaning close to one another. ﴿And gardens﴾ of ﴿grapes, and olives, and pomegranates, similar﴾ in their leaves, which is a *hal* (circumstantial clause), ﴿and dissimilar﴾ in their fruit. ﴿Look﴾, O you who are addressed, with a look of contemplation, ﴿at its fruit﴾, read with *fatha* on the *tha'* and the *mim*, and also with *damma* on both, and it is the plural of *thamara*, like *shajara* and *shajar*, and *khashaba* and *khashab*, ﴿when it bears fruit﴾, at the first appearance of it, how it is, ﴿and its ripening﴾, until it matures, when it ripens, how it returns. ﴿Surely in that are signs﴾, proofs of His power, exalted is He, over the resurrection and other things, ﴿for a people who believe﴾. They are singled out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from them in faith, unlike the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 100:

﴿And they made for Allah﴾ the second object (maf'ul thani), and ﴿partners﴾ is the first object (maf'ul awwal), and ﴿the jinn﴾ is substituted for it (yubdal minhu), since they obeyed them in worshipping idols. ﴿And﴾ [while] He ﴿created them﴾, so how could they be partners? ﴿And they invented﴾ (kharaqu), with both the light and the emphatic recitation (bi-l-takhfif wa-l-tashdid), meaning they fabricated ﴿for Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾, since they said: Uzayr is the son of Allah, and the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, declaring Him far exalted above that, ﴿and exalted is He above what they describe﴾, namely that He has a child.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 101:

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ — He is their Innovator (mubdi'uhuma) without any precedent example (mithal) preceding it. ﴿How can He have a child when He has no consort?﴾ — i.e., how could He have a son when He has no wife (ṣāḥiba: a wife). ﴿And He created all things﴾ — it is within His nature to create. ﴿That is God, your Lord; there is no god but Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him﴾ — make Him one (waḥḥidūhu). ﴿And He is Guardian over all things﴾ — Preserver (ḥafīẓ) of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 103:

﴿No vision can perceive Him﴾, i.e., cannot see Him. This is specific to the vision of the believers of Him in the Hereafter, based on His saying, exalted is He: "Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord" and the hadith of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim): "Verily, you will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night of the full moon." It was also said that what is meant is: "No vision can encompass Him." ﴿And He perceives the vision﴾, i.e., He sees it while it does not see Him, and it is not permissible for anyone else that vision perceives him while he does not perceive it, or that he encompasses it in knowledge. ﴿And He is the Subtle (al-Latif)﴾ toward His friends (awliya'), ﴿the All-Aware (al-Khabir)﴾ of them.

Say, O Muhammad, to them: ﴿There has come to you clear evidences (basa'ir)﴾ proofs ﴿from your Lord. So whoever sees﴾ whoever sees them and believes ﴿it is for his own self﴾ he sees, because the reward of his seeing is for him ﴿And whoever is blind﴾ to them, and goes astray ﴿it is to his own detriment﴾ the harm of his misguidance ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾ a watcher over your deeds; I am only a warner.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 105:

﴿And thus﴾ as We have explained what has been mentioned, ﴿We display﴾ We make clear ﴿the verses﴾ so that they may take heed, ﴿and that they may say﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, at the end of the matter, ﴿You have studied﴾ you have discussed with the People of the Book. And in another reading, "you have studied" means you have read the books of those who came before, and brought this from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 106:

﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, i.e., the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 107:

﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him. And We have not made you a watcher over them﴾ (i.e., a guardian) ruling over them, so that you would requite them for their deeds, ﴿and you are not a guardian over them﴾ (i.e., a compeller), so that you would force them to faith. And this was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 108:

﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah﴾ — i.e., the idols — ﴿lest they revile Allah in enmity﴾ — transgressing and wrongfully — ﴿without knowledge﴾ — i.e., out of their ignorance of Allah. ﴿Thus﴾ — just as We have made this [conduct] appealing to these people, what they are upon — ﴿We have made appealing to every community their deeds﴾ — of good and evil — so let them do them. ﴿Then to their Lord is their return﴾ — in the Hereafter — ﴿and He will inform them of what they used to do﴾ — and so He will recompense them for it.

They swore by God with their most emphatic oaths (ﷺ not applicable) — rather: "And they swore by God with the utmost effort of their oaths," meaning the Meccan unbelievers, "that if a sign came to them" of what they had proposed, "they would surely believe in it." Say: "Signs are only with God; He sends them down as He wills, and I am only a warner." "And what makes you aware" — that is, what makes you know about their faith when it comes — "that when it comes they will not believe?" — i.e., you do not know that — "because of what has preceded in My knowledge."

In another reading with the ta' (تاء), it is addressed to the unbelievers as a direct address, and in another reading with the fath of anna (أنَّ), it carries the meaning of "perhaps" (لعلَّ), or it is governed by what precedes it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 110:

﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes away﴾ — We divert their hearts from the truth, so they do not comprehend it; and their eyes from it, so they do not perceive it, and so they do not believe. ﴿As they did not believe in it﴾ — i.e., in what was sent down of the signs ﴿the first time. And We leave them﴾ — We abandon them ﴿in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ — hesitating, bewildered.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 111:

﴿Even if We had sent down the angels to them, and the dead had spoken to them﴾ as they demanded, ﴿and We had gathered together against them every thing face to face﴾ — qubulan, read with two dammas, is the plural of qabil, meaning in groups, group by group; and read with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', it means facing them, in direct sight, so that they would witness to the truth of you — ﴿they would not have believed﴾ because of what had preceded in the knowledge of Allah ﴿unless﴾ but [it would happen] ﴿that Allah wills﴾ their faith, so that they would believe; ﴿but most of them are ignorant﴾ of this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 112:

﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn, some of them inspiring to others ornamented speech as deception.﴾ Like We have appointed these as your enemies (ويُبْدَل مِنهُ: and "devils" is a substitution from it). ﴿Devils﴾ (shayatin): rebellious ones (مَرَدَة) ﴿of mankind and jinn﴾. ﴿Inspiring﴾ (yuhi): whispering (يُوَسْوِس) ﴿to one another﴾ (ba'duhum ila ba'd) ﴿ornamented speech﴾ (zukhruf al-qawl): embellished (مُمَوَّهه) with falsehood ﴿as deception﴾ (ghurura): meaning, so that they might deceive them. ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾: i.e., the aforementioned inspiring. ﴿So leave them﴾ (fadharhum): leave alone the disbelievers ﴿and what they fabricate﴾ of disbelief and other things that have been made attractive to them. This was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 113:

﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾ is conjoined to "deception" (ghurūran), meaning: they incline (tamīlu) ﴿to it﴾, i.e., the adornment (al-zukhruf), ﴿the hearts (af'ida)﴾, i.e., the hearts (qulūb) ﴿of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit (liyaqtarifū)﴾, i.e., acquire (yaktasibū) ﴿what they are committing (muqtarifūn)﴾ of sins, so that they will be punished for it.

Revealed when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to appoint a judge between him and them. Say: ﴿Shall I seek other than Allah as a judge?﴾ i.e., seek [as] a judge, deciding between me and you. ﴿And it is He who has sent down to you the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿explained in detail﴾, clarifying within it the truth from falsehood. ﴿And those whom We gave the Book﴾, the Torah, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions, ﴿know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth. So do not be among the doubters﴾, those who have doubt concerning it. The purpose of this is to affirm to the disbelievers that it is the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 115:

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ by the rulings and the promises, ﴿in truth and in justice﴾. صِدْقًا وعَدْلًا is in the accusative as a *tamyīz* (specification, a noun clarifying the sense of the preceding statement). ﴿None can alter His words﴾ by deficiency or substitution, ﴿and He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what is said, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what is done.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 116:

﴿And if you obey most of those on earth﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾, His religion. ﴿They follow nothing but assumption﴾ (in their disputing with you regarding the matter of carrion, when they say: "What Allah has killed is more deserving that you eat it than what you have killed"). ﴿And they do nothing but guess﴾, i.e., they lie in that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 117:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing﴾, meaning, knowing (ʿalim) ﴿of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided﴾, so He will recompense each of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 118:

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned﴾ — i.e., that which was slaughtered in His name.

And what is [the matter] with you that you should not eat of [the slaughtered animals] over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, when He has already explained in detail (fuṣṣila), with the verb in both places read in the passive and in the active voice, what He has forbidden to you? ﴿For you is what He has forbidden to you﴾ in another verse: ﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾, ﴿except what you are compelled to﴾ [eat], which is also lawful for you. The meaning is: there is nothing preventing you from eating what has been mentioned [the name of Allah over it], since He has made clear to you what is forbidden to eat, and this [animal over which the name was mentioned] is not among it.

﴿And indeed many lead astray﴾, with the ya of yuḍillūna read with a fatha (yaḍillūna, "they go astray") or with a damma (yuḍillūna, "they lead astray"), ﴿by their desires﴾, that is, by what their souls desire of making carrion and other things lawful, ﴿without knowledge﴾ upon which they rely in that. ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors﴾, those who exceed the limits.

﴿And leave﴾ اُتْرُكُوا ﴿the outward and the inward of sin﴾ their public and their secret. As for al-ithm (sin), it has been said to mean fornication, and it has been said to mean every act of disobedience. ﴿Indeed those who earn sin will be recompensed﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿for what they used to commit﴾ يَكْتَسِبُونَ (they would acquire).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 121:

﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾, meaning, [an animal] that died [of itself] or was slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. Otherwise, what a Muslim slaughters without mentioning [Allah's name] over it, whether deliberately or forgetfully, is lawful. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Shafi'i (the eponymous founder of the Shafi'i school of law) also held it. ﴿And indeed it﴾, i.e., eating from it, ﴿is grave disobedience﴾, meaning, departure from what is lawful. ﴿And indeed the devils inspire﴾, i.e., whisper, ﴿to their allies﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿to dispute with you﴾ regarding the permissibility of carrion, ﴿and if you obey them﴾ in this.

It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and others: ﴿Is one who was dead⁠ —⁠ in disbelief ⁠— then We gave him life⁠ —⁠ with guidance ⁠— and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, discerning the truth from other than it, which is faith; ﴿like one who is in the darknesses, not coming out of them?﴾ Here "mathaluhu" (its likeness) has "mathal" as an extra word, meaning "like one who is," that is, the disbeliever. ﴿Thus﴾, just as faith was made attractive to the believers, ﴿the deeds they used to do was made attractive to the disbelievers﴾, namely disbelief and sins.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 123:

﴿And thus﴾ just as We made the dissolute (fussaq) of Makkah its greatest ones (akabir), ﴿We placed in every town greatest ones of its criminals﴾ ﴿so that they may scheme therein﴾ by hindering (al-sadd) from faith (al-iman), ﴿but they scheme only against themselves﴾ because its harm falls upon them, ﴿and they perceive it not﴾ of that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 124:

﴿And when a sign comes to them﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿confirming the truth of the Prophet﴾ (ﷺ), ﴿they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of God"﴾, namely prophethood and revelation sent down to us, ﴿because we are greater in wealth and older in years﴾. ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾, with the plural and the singular readings. "Where" (ḥaythu) is the object of a verb implied by "knows best" (aʿlam): i.e., He knows the suitable place to put it, so He places it there, and these people are not worthy of it. ﴿Those who committed crime﴾ by this statement of theirs ﴿will be struck with humiliation (ṣaghār) before God, and a severe punishment for what they used to scheme﴾, i.e., because of their scheming.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 125:

﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾, by casting into his heart a light, so that it opens up and accepts it, as has been related in a hadith. ﴿And whomever He wills to leave astray﴾, Allah ﴿makes his breast constricted﴾, (with the letter ḍād either lightened or intensified in recitation) so that it refuses to accept it, ﴿constricted﴾, intensely tight, with the rāʾ vowelled with kasra as an adjective (ḥarajan, i.e. ḥaraj as a descriptive form) and with fatḥa as a verbal noun (maṣdar) of the verb waṣafa, in which there is emphasis (mubālagha). ﴿As though he were climbing up into the sky﴾, and in another recitation yaṣṣāʿadu, and in both the tāʾ of the original root is assimilated into the ṣād; and in another reading it is with a sukūn on the tāʾ. ﴿Into the sky﴾, when he is burdened with faith, because of its severity upon him. ﴿Thus﴾, in this manner of placing, ﴿Allah places the filth﴾, meaning the punishment or the Satan, i.e. He empowers it over him.

This is the Tafsir al-Jalalayn, the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 6, verse 126:

﴿And this﴾ which you are upon, O Muhammad, is the ﴿path﴾ (ṣirāṭ), the way, ﴿of your Lord, straight﴾, with no crookedness in it. Its being in the accusative (naṣb) is as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) emphasizing the sentence, and the operator (ʿāmil) governing it is the sense of pointing (ishāra). ﴿We have detailed﴾ (faṣṣalnā), i.e. made clear, ﴿the signs for a people who remember﴾ (yadhdhakkarūn). In it there is idghām (assimilation) of the tā' of the original form into the dhāl, i.e. ﴿who take heed﴾ (yattaʿiẓūn), and they were singled out for mention because they are the ones who benefit.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 127:

﴿For them is the abode of peace﴾ i.e., the abode of peace, which is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 128:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the day﴾ when ﴿He will gather them all﴾ (read with the nun and the ya', i.e., Allah gathers the creation) ﴿all together﴾. And it will be said to them: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind﴾ by your misguiding them. ﴿And their allies among mankind will say﴾ (those who obeyed them): ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another﴾: mankind benefited from the jinn's adornment of desires for them, and the jinn benefited from mankind's obedience to them. ﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, and this is an expression of regret from them. ﴿He will say﴾, exalted is He, to them through the tongue of the angels: ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾ (your refuge), ﴿abiding therein forever, except what Allah wills﴾ of the times when they go out to drink the boiling water, for He has removed them from it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then indeed your return is to the Blazing Fire﴾. And it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that this exception concerns those whom Allah knows will believe, so the word "min" here has the meaning of... ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise﴾ in His doing, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of His creation.

And thus (كَذَلِكَ), as We let the disobedient among mankind and jinn enjoy one another, [﴿نُولِي﴾] We set (نُولِي), from wilaya (guardianship/ruling authority), [﴿بَعْض الظّالِمِينَ بَعْضًا﴾] some of the wrongdoers over others, i.e., over one another (أيْ عَلى بَعْض), [﴿بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾] because of what they used to earn, namely the acts of disobedience (مِن المَعاصِي).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 130:

﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ That is, from among your whole company, meaning some of you, which is true of mankind; or [it means] messengers of the jinn, their warners, who would hear the speech of the messengers and then convey it to their people. ﴿Relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this your Day﴾ ﴿They will say, "We testify against ourselves."﴾ That is, that they had conveyed [the message] to us. ﴿And the worldly life deceived them﴾ so they did not believe.

﴿Dhalika﴾ means: that is, the sending of the messengers. ﴿Anna﴾: the lam (of causation) is implied, and it is the light (mukhaffafah) form of anna; that is, because ﴿your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly﴾, from among them, ﴿while their people were unaware﴾, and no messenger had been sent to them to make things clear for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 132:

﴿And for each﴾ of those who do deeds ﴿are degrees﴾ as a recompense ﴿for what they have done﴾ of good and evil ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾, with the ya' and the ta' (i.e., read as yaʿmalūna, "they do," and taʿmalūna, "you [plural] do").

Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani) above His creation and their worship, Lord of mercy (dhu al-rahma). If He wills, He can remove you, O people of Mecca, by destruction, and make successors after you of whatever He wills from creation, just as He produced you from the offspring of another people (qawm akharin) whom He destroyed. But He has kept you alive out of mercy for you.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah al-An'am (6), verse 134:

﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾ of the Hour and the punishment ﴿is coming﴾ without doubt, ﴿and you cannot escape﴾ (mu'jizin) — you cannot get away from Our punishment.

Say (to them): ﴿O my people, act according to your station﴾, that is, your state, ﴿indeed I am acting according to my state﴾. ﴿So you will come to know who﴾, here *man* (مَن) is a *mawṣūla* (relative pronoun) functioning as the object of the knowing (*maf'ūl al-'ilm*, the direct object of the verb "to know"), ﴿will have the good end of the abode﴾, that is, the praiseworthy outcome in the Hereafter: whether it will be us or you. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾, that is, will not prosper, referring to the disbelievers.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 6, verse 136:

﴿And they assigned﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿to God a share of what He created﴾ (dhara'a: created) ﴿of the tilth﴾ (al-harth: the crops) ﴿and the livestock﴾ ﴿a share﴾, which they spend on the guests and the poor; ﴿and to their associates a share﴾, which they spend on their custodians (sadana, sing. sadin: keepers of the idols). ﴿So they say: "This is for God," by their claim﴾, with fatha and with damma (in the reading of bi-za‘mihim), ﴿and this is for our associates."﴾ So whenever something fell from God's share into the associates' share, they picked it up, and whenever something from the associates' share fell into God's share, they left it. They would also say, "God is free of need of this," as the One, exalted is He, said: ﴿So what is for their associates does not reach God﴾, i.e., does not reach His side, ﴿and what is for God reaches their associates.﴾ ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ (sa'a: evil is; bi'sa: what) ﴿their judgement this.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 137:

﴿And thus﴾ as what was mentioned was made attractive to them, ﴿their partners [from among the jinn] made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ by burying them alive, ﴿their partners﴾ from among the jinn. The word "partners" is in the nominative (بِالرَّفْعِ) as the subject (فاعِل) of "zuyyina" (was made attractive). In another reading (qira'a), it is passive in form (بِبِنائِهِ لِلْمَفْعُولِ), with "qatl" (killing) in the nominative (ورَفْع قَتْل) and "al-awlad" (the children) in the accusative (ونَصْب الأَوْلاد) as its object, and "shurakaihim" (their partners) in the genitive (وجَرّ شُرَكائِهِمْ) by being its annexed noun (بِإضافَتِهِ). In this reading there is a separation (الفَصْل) between the annexed noun (al-mudaf) and the noun it is annexed to (al-mudaf ilayhi) by the object (بِالمَفْعُولِ), which does no harm (ولا يَضُرّ). The attribution of the killing to the partners is because they commanded it (وإضافَة القَتْل إلى الشُّرَكاء لِأَمْرِهِمْ بِهِ). ﴿So that they might destroy them﴾ (لِيُرْدُوهُمْ), i.e., ruin them (يُهْلِكُوهُمْ), ﴿and so that they might confuse them﴾ (ولِيَلْبِسُوا), i.e., mix them up (يَخْلِطُوا).

Qur'an 6:138: "And they say, 'These cattle and crops are forbidden (ḥijr) — none may eat of them except whom we will,' by their claim — and [there are] cattle whose backs are forbidden, [and] cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah — a fabrication against Him. He will recompense them for what they used to fabricate."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti):

"And they say, 'These are cattle and tilth, ḥijr' — forbidden — 'none may eat of them except whom We will' — of the attendants of the idols and others — 'by their claim' — meaning, they have no proof for it. 'And cattle whose backs have been forbidden' — so they are not ridden, like the sawā'ib and the ḥawāmī. 'And cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah' — at the time of slaughtering them; rather they mention the names of their idols, and they attribute that to Allah — 'a fabrication against Him.' 'He will recompense them for what they used to fabricate' against Him."

Notes on terms (first occurrence):
- Ḥijr (ḥijr): a term meaning "forbidden" or "prohibited," here referring to a sacred restriction the pagans placed on certain livestock and crops.
- Sawā'ib (sawā'ib, sing. sā'iba): free-roaming camels set loose for idols, and not ridden or milked.
- Ḥawāmī (ḥawāmī, sing. ḥāmī): animals (often camels) dedicated and protected from use, in pre-Islamic practice.

"And they say: 'What is in the wombs of these livestock' — the forbidden ones, namely the sawa'ib and the bahair — '[is] pure (khalisah) for our males and forbidden to our wives,'" i.e., the women. "'But if it is dead (maytah)'" — with both the nominative and accusative readings, and with the verb feminine and masculine — "'then they are partners in it.'" "He will recompense them for their description" — that is, for that attribution of permissibility and prohibition — i.e., their recompense. "Indeed He is Wise" in His creation, "All-Knowing" of His creatures.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 6, verse 140:

﴿Certainly lost are those who killed﴾ (qatalū, read with both the light and the intensive forms) ﴿their children﴾ by burying them alive (al-wa'd) ﴿out of foolishness﴾ (jahlan, ignorance) ﴿without knowledge, and forbade what Allah had provided for them﴾ of what has been mentioned.

﴿And it is He who produced﴾ created ﴿gardens﴾ orchards ﴿trellised﴾ spread out upon the ground, like melons, ﴿and untrellised﴾ rising upon a stalk, like palm trees, ﴿and the palm trees and crops, varying in their produce﴾ He produced their fruit and grain, differing in appearance and taste, ﴿and the olives and pomegranates, similar﴾ their leaves being alike ﴿and dissimilar﴾ in their taste. ﴿Eat of their fruit when it bears fruit﴾ before it ripens, ﴿and give its due﴾ its zakat (obligatory almsgiving) ﴿on the day of its harvest﴾ الحَصاد read with fatḥ and with kasr on the ḥāʾ, of the tenth (ʿushr) or half of it, ﴿and do not be wasteful﴾ by giving all of it, so that nothing remains for your dependents, ﴿indeed He does not love the wasteful﴾ those who exceed what has been set as their limit.

And He produced from the cattle [that which is] a burden-bearer (ḥamūlah), fit for being carried upon, like the large camels, and [that which is] a bed (farsh), not fit for that, like the young camels and the sheep and goats. They were named "furush" (beds) because they are like beds for the earth, being close to it.

﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps (khuṭuwāt) of Shaytan.﴾ Its paths (ṭarā'iq) of forbidding and permitting. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ Evident in enmity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 143:

﴿Eight pairs﴾: kinds, in apposition to "carrying animals" and "flat-lying ones" (ḥamūlah wa-furushan). ﴿Of sheep﴾ two, a pair: ﴿two﴾, a male and a female. ﴿And of goats﴾ (with the fatḥa and the sukūn on the mīm, both readings) ﴿two﴾. ﴿Say﴾: O Muhammad, to those who forbade the males of the livestock at one time and their females at another, and attributed that to God: ﴿Is it the two males﴾ of the sheep and the goats ﴿that He has forbidden﴾ to you, ﴿or the two females﴾ of them? ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾, whether male or female. ﴿Tell me with knowledge﴾ about the manner of forbidding this, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ about it, meaning: from where did the prohibition come? If it is from the maleness, then all males are forbidden; or from the femaleness, then all females are forbidden; or from what the womb contains, then the two (the pair) are forbidden, so from where comes the specification? The interrogative is for denunciation (al-inkār).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 144:

﴿And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you?﴾ Rather, ﴿you were witnesses﴾ present, ﴿when Allah enjoined this upon you﴾ the prohibition, so that you adopted it! No, rather you are liars in it. ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ regarding that?, meaning: no one, ﴿than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ concerning that.

Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, except that it be carrion" (with the verb read with ya' and ta', and "carrion" in the accusative; in another reading it is in the nominative with the verb in the yā' form) "or blood poured forth" (flowing, unlike other blood, such as the liver and the spleen) "or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is an abomination" (ḥarām), "or" except that it be "a sinful offering over which other than Allah has been invoked" (i.e., slaughtered in the name of other than Allah). "But whoever is compelled" (to something of what has been mentioned, and eats it) "without being rebellious or transgressing, indeed your Lord is Forgiving" (of what he ate) "and Merciful" (to him). And to what has been mentioned, by the Sunnah, is added every animal with fangs among the predators and every bird with talons.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 146:

﴿And upon those who were Jews﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿We forbade every animal with claws﴾, which is that whose toes are not separated, such as camels and ostriches, ﴿and from cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat﴾, the thurub (the fat covering the entrails) and the fat of the kidneys, ﴿except what their backs carry﴾, i.e., what clings to them of it, ﴿or﴾ what is carried by ﴿the entrails﴾, the intestines, plural of hawaya or hawiya, ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾ of it, which is the fat of the rump, for it was made lawful to them. ﴿That﴾ prohibition ﴿We recompensed them with﴾ ﴿for their rebellion﴾, because of their wrongdoing, with what preceded in Surat an-Nisa'. ﴿And indeed, We are truthful﴾ in Our reports and Our promises.

ۚ "If they deny you" regarding what you have brought, "then say," to them, "Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy," in that He has not hastened punishment upon you, and in this is gentleness in calling them to faith; "but His punishment will not be turned back" from the people, once it has come.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 148:

﴿The ones who associated partners [with Allah] will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him], nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything."﴾ Their saying "we" [refers to them]. ﴿Nor would our fathers [have associated]. Nor would we have forbidden anything.﴾ So our associating and our forbidding are by His will, and thus He is pleased with it. ﴿Thus﴾ just as these [people] denied [their messengers], ﴿those before them denied [their messengers]﴾, ﴿until they tasted Our might﴾, Our punishment. ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge?"﴾ [knowledge] that Allah is pleased with that ﴿so that you may bring it out for us﴾, meaning you have no knowledge. ﴿You follow only conjecture﴾ in that matter ﴿and you are only guessing﴾, lying in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 149:

﴿Say﴾ (O Muhammad to them): If you have no proof, ﴿then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof﴾, the complete one, ﴿so had He willed﴾ your guidance,

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 150:

﴿Say, "Bring forth your witnesses who testify that Allah has prohibited this."﴾ (Bring forth) produce ﴿your witnesses who testify that Allah has prohibited this﴾ — this which you have prohibited — ﴿And if they testify, then do not testify with them, nor follow the desires of those who denied Our signs, and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ — they worship others (yushrikūna) alongside Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 151:

﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you"﴾ I will recite (ut'lu, "recite") ﴿what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ — "an" here is explanatory (mufassira) ﴿that you associate nothing with Him, and [be good] to your parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children﴾ by burying them alive (al-wa'd) ﴿out of﴾ on account of ﴿poverty﴾ — a need you fear ﴿We provide for you and for them. And do not approach the abominations﴾ the major sins, such as fornication ﴿whether apparent or concealed﴾ i.e., their open and their secret forms ﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾ such as retaliation (qawad), the punishment for apostasy, and stoning the married adulterer ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you, so that you may understand﴾ may reflect.

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾, i.e., by the manner that is best, which is what contains his welfare, ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾ by reaching puberty (*ihtilam*). ﴿And give full measure and full weight with justice﴾, i.e., with equity and by abstaining from defrauding (*bakhs*). ﴿We do not burden any soul except within its capacity﴾, i.e., its ability in that. So if he errs in the measure and the weight, and Allah knows the soundness of his intention, there is no blame upon him, as is related in a hadith. ﴿And when you speak﴾ in a judgment or otherwise, ﴿be just﴾ with truthfulness, ﴿even if it concerns a near relative﴾, i.e., a kinship tie. ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember﴾ with the *tashdid* (تَذَكَّرُونَ), meaning you take heed, and with the *sukun* (تَذْكُرُونَ).

**"Wa-anna"** (وَأَنَّ), with a fatḥa, is read on the assumption of an implied lām (the lām of purpose, "because"). With a kasra, it is read as a new sentence, an *isti'nāf* (resumption, beginning a fresh statement). ﴿And that is﴾ **"hadha"** (هَذا), "this," refers to what I enjoined upon you, ﴿My path, straight﴾. **"Mustaqīman"** (مُسْتَقِيمًا) is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) describing the path. ﴿So follow it, and do not follow the ways﴾, meaning the paths that oppose it, ﴿lest you be separated﴾. In **"fa-tafarraqa"** (فَتَفَرَّقَ), one of the two tā's has been elided, so the verb is **"tatafarraqa"** (تَتَفَرَّقَ) in its original form; **"tamīl"** (تَمِيل) means ﴿it leads you astray﴾ ﴿from His way﴾, meaning His religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 154:

﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾, meaning the Torah. The "thumma" (then) here is for ordering the reports (lit. "for the sequence of the news"), not of time. ﴿Complete [favour]﴾ for ﴿him who did good﴾, by carrying it out. ﴿And a detailed explanation﴾, a clarification ﴿of everything﴾ that is needed in religion, ﴿and guidance and mercy; that perhaps they﴾, i.e. the Children of Israel, ﴿would believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾, i.e. the Resurrection.
This is the Qur'an, a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it, O people of Makkah, by acting upon what is in it, and fear [God by avoiding] disbelief.

We sent it down lest you say: "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups," the Jews and the Christians, "before us; and indeed we were, regarding their study," i.e., their recitation, "unaware," because we did not know it, since it was not in our language.

Or lest you should say: "If the Book had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they." ﴿For that reason﴾ because of the quickness of our minds, ﴿there has certainly come to you a clear proof﴾ an explanation ﴿from your Lord, and guidance and mercy﴾ for whoever follows it. ﴿Then who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of God and turns away from them?﴾ That is, no one is more unjust, ﴿turned away﴾ from them ﴿We will repay those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment﴾ that is, the most severe of it.

﴿Do they await﴾ (meaning: what are the deniers waiting for?) ﴿except that the angels come to them﴾ (read with the letter *tāʾ* and with the letter *yāʾ*, بِالتّاءِ والياء) ﴿to take their souls﴾ ﴿or that your Lord comes﴾, i.e., His command, meaning His punishment ﴿or that some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, i.e., its signs that indicate the Hour ﴿on the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, and these are the rising of the sun from its west, as in the hadith of the two *Sahihs* (al-Bukhari and Muslim) ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before﴾. The clause (*al-jumlah*, the grammatical sentence) is a description of the soul (*nafs*) ﴿or﴾ a soul that had not ﴿earned good through its faith﴾, meaning obedience. That is, its repentance will not benefit it, as in the hadith. ﴿Say: Wait﴾ for one of these things ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 159:

﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion﴾ by their differing over it, so they took up part of it and left off part of it, ﴿and became sects﴾ (firaq) in that matter. In another reading, it is fara-qu (they separated), meaning they abandoned their religion which they were commanded to follow, and they are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿You have nothing to do with them﴾ (laste minhum fi shay'), meaning, do not confront them. ﴿Their affair is with Allah﴾ (innama amrahum ila Allah), He will take charge of it. ﴿Then He will inform them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿of what they used to do﴾, so that He will recompense them for it. And this verse is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 160:

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), ﴿for him is ten times the like thereof﴾, i.e., the reward of ten good deeds. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with the like thereof﴾, i.e., its recompense. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, meaning they will not have anything of their recompense diminished.
Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path," ﴿a right religion﴾, upright (مُسْتَقِيمًا).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 162:

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my rites of sacrifice﴾ my worship, including the pilgrimage and other than it, ﴿and my living﴾ my life, ﴿and my dying﴾ my death.
"There is no partner for Him" in that [matter], "and of that I have been commanded," i.e., of the Oneness [of God], "and I am the first of the Muslims" of this community.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 6, verse 164:

﴿Say, "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah," ﴾ meaning, a deity; i.e., I do not seek other than Him, ﴿while He is the Lord﴾ the Owner ﴿of all things? And no soul earns [any sin] except against itself﴾ [i.e., its sin falls only upon itself], ﴿and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ [meaning, no soul bearing sin (wazira) bears the sin (wizr) of another soul].

And He it is who made you successors (khalā'if, plural of khalīfah) upon the earth, and raised some of you above others in degrees, by wealth, rank and other things, that He may test you in what He has given you, i.e. has bestowed upon you, so that the obedient among you and the disobedient may be made manifest. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, for whoever disobeys Him; and indeed He is Forgiving, to the believers, Merciful to them.
